learn: Hola, me llamo... tells your name. Tengo siete años tells your age.
Soy de Arizona means I am from Arizona.
Put it together: Hola, me llamo Sam. Tengo siete años. Soy de Tucson.
lessons.try: Write and say three sentences about yourself.

learn: ¿Cómo te llamas? asks the name. ¿Cuántos años tienes? asks the age.
¿De dónde eres? asks where someone is from.
Question words: cómo (how), cuántos (how many), dónde (where), qué (what).
lessons.try: Interview a family member with all three questions.

learn: El amigo is a boy friend and la amiga is a girl friend. Los amigos are friends.
Mi amiga se llama Lucía means my friend's name is Lucía.
¿Quieres jugar? means do you want to play?
check: Mi amiga se llama Lucía means...
lessons.try: Ask a friend ¿quieres jugar? at recess.

learn: ¿De dónde eres? Where are you from?
Soy de Arizona. Soy de México.
Soy de means I am from.
check: Soy de México means I am from...
lessons.try: Ask three classmates where they are from.

lessons.t: What Do You Like to Do?
learn: ¿Qué te gusta hacer? What do you like to do?
Find friends with the same likes.
check: Me gusta dibujar means I like to...
lessons.try: Find a classmate who likes the same thing as you.
Write two kind words about a friend.

learn: ¿Quieres jugar? Do you want to play?
lessons.try: Use three playground phrases at recess.

learn: Write your name, age and likes.
Sign: Tu amigo or Tu amiga.
check: A pen pal letter tells your name, age and...
lessons.try: Write a short pen pal letter.
Interview a new friend.

learn: Counting by tens is fast and helps with big numbers.
Cincuenta sounds like cinco because it is five tens.
lessons.try: Count by tens to cincuenta while clapping.

learn: Twenty-one is veintiuno. Twenty-two is veintidós. Twenty-five is veinticinco.
The 20s are written as one word.
lessons.try: Count from veintiuno to treinta.

learn: After 30, we use y (and): treinta y uno (31), treinta y dos (32).
Cuarenta y cinco is 45. Cuarenta y nueve is 49.
These are written as three words.
lessons.try: Write your house number or a number you like up to 50 in Spanish words.
Count by fives with a partner.

learn: Cuesta veinte pesos: it costs twenty pesos.
check: Cuesta cuarenta pesos means it costs...
lessons.try: Play shop with prices to 50 pesos.

learn: Treinta y dos = 3 tens and 2 ones.
Y joins tens and ones from 31 up.
check: The word joining tens and ones is...
lessons.try: Build and say five numbers.
Add tens with bundles of sticks.
Make up a number riddle.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Numbers to 50
lessons.try: Number market game.

learn: Enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio.
Julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre.
Like days, months start with a small letter in Spanish.
lessons.try: Sing or chant the twelve months.

learn: Hoy es lunes, el cinco de octubre means today is Monday, October 5.
In Spanish we say the number first, then the month.
The first of the month is el primero.
check: In Spanish dates, what comes first?
lessons.try: Say today's full date in Spanish.

learn: ¿Cuándo es tu cumpleaños? means when is your birthday?
Mi cumpleaños es el doce de marzo means my birthday is March 12.
check: ¿Cuándo es tu cumpleaños? asks about your...
lessons.try: Ask five people when their birthday is and write the dates in Spanish.

learn: Los + day means every that day.
lessons.try: Write your weekly schedule in Spanish.
Make a holiday calendar.

learn: The first day of the month: el primero.
Line up and say your place.
lessons.try: Line up and say ordinal numbers.
Make a class birthday bar graph.

learn: En enero hace frío (in many places).
lessons.try: Match months to weather where you live.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: The Calendar
lessons.try: Calendar quiz game.

learn: La casa is the house. La cocina is the kitchen. El baño is the bathroom.
La sala is the living room. El dormitorio or el cuarto is the bedroom.
El jardín is the yard or garden.
lessons.try: Draw a map of your home and label each room in Spanish.

learn: La cama is the bed. La mesa is the table. La puerta is the door. La ventana is the window.
El sofá is the sofa. La lámpara is the lamp.
Hay means there is or there are. Hay una cama en el cuarto.
lessons.try: Say three things that hay in your bedroom.

learn: En means in or on. Debajo de means under. Encima de means on top of.
El gato está debajo de la mesa. The cat is under the table.
lessons.try: Hide a toy and give clues in Spanish: está debajo de, está encima de.

learn: La cama (bed), la mesa (table), la silla (chair).
lessons.try: Draw your room and label furniture.

learn: Arriba (upstairs or up), abajo (downstairs or down).
lessons.try: Describe where rooms are in a house picture.

learn: Hago mi cama: I make my bed.
Lavo los platos: I wash the dishes.
Saco la basura: I take out the trash.
check: Hago mi cama means I make my...
Lavo los platos means I wash the...
lessons.try: Make a chore chart in Spanish.

learn: Encima de (on top of), debajo de (under).
Al lado de (next to), dentro de (inside).
The cat is debajo de la mesa.
lessons.try: Hide a toy and describe where it is.

learn: Mi casa ideal tiene una piscina (pool).
lessons.try: Design and describe a dream house.
House tour presentation.

learn: La cabeza, los ojos, la nariz, la boca, las orejas, los brazos, las manos, las piernas, los pies.
El estómago is the stomach. Los dientes are the teeth.
Me duele means it hurts me. Me duele la cabeza means my head hurts.
lessons.try: Play Simón dice with body parts.

learn: Lávate las manos means wash your hands. Cepíllate los dientes means brush your teeth.
Duerme means sleep. Children need lots of sleep every night.
Healthy food, water, sleep and exercise keep us strong.
lessons.try: Make a healthy habits poster in Spanish.

learn: El doctor or la doctora helps when we are sick. Estoy enfermo means I am sick.
Tengo fiebre means I have a fever. Tengo tos means I have a cough.
lessons.try: Act out a visit to the doctor with a toy.

learn: Corro (I run), salto (I jump), nado (I swim).
check: El ejercicio es bueno means exercise is...
lessons.try: Lead a Spanish exercise warm-up.

learn: Veo (I see), oigo (I hear), huelo (I smell).
check: Los cinco sentidos means the five...
lessons.try: Do a five senses walk.

learn: Duermo ocho horas (I sleep eight hours).
lessons.try: Draw your bedtime routine.

learn: Estoy enfermo or enferma: I'm sick.
Tengo fiebre: I have a fever.
Tengo tos: I have a cough.
lessons.try: Role-play telling the nurse how you feel.
Make a healthy habits poster.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Body and Health
lessons.try: Doctor's office skit.

learn: La camisa, la camiseta (T-shirt), los pantalones, la falda (skirt), el vestido (dress).
Los zapatos, las botas (boots), la gorra (cap), los lentes (glasses).
Llevo una camiseta roja means I am wearing a red T-shirt.
lessons.try: Describe what three family members are wearing.

learn: Colors change to match the word: un vestido rojo, una camisa roja.
Words with el usually take colors ending in o, and words with la take colors ending in a.
Some colors stay the same: verde, azul, gris.
lessons.try: Write four sentences: un zapato negro, una falda negra...

learn: Me pongo means I put on. Me pongo los zapatos.
Primero means first. Después means after. Al final means at the end.
Primero, me pongo los calcetines. Después, me pongo los zapatos.
lessons.try: Tell the order you get dressed using primero and después.
Describe your shoes and backpack.

learn: La camisa roja; el sombrero rojo.
Colours ending in o change to a for feminine words.
lessons.try: Fix five colour phrases.

learn: Many schools in Latin America have uniforms.
Camisa blanca, falda o pantalón azul.
check: A uniform is clothing that is...
lessons.try: Draw and label a school uniform.

learn: Me queda bien: it fits me well.
lessons.try: Role-play a clothes shop.
Hold a Spanish fashion show.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Clothes and Colours
lessons.try: Dress the paper doll in Spanish.

learn: El plato is the plate. El vaso is the cup or glass. La cuchara is the spoon. El tenedor is the fork.
¿Me pasas la sal, por favor? means can you pass me the salt, please?
lessons.try: Set the table and name each thing in Spanish.

learn: Tortillas are flat breads made from corn or flour.
Tacos, tamales, enchiladas and frijoles (beans) are popular foods.
Many of these foods are enjoyed in Arizona too.
lessons.try: Help make a simple quesadilla with a grown-up and name the foods.

learn: Quisiera means I would like. Quisiera un taco, por favor.
¿Algo más? means anything else? Nada más means nothing else.
La cuenta is the bill at a restaurant.
lessons.try: Play restaurant: one person orders and one serves, all in Spanish.
Vote for the favourite snack in Spanish.
Make guacamole following Spanish steps.
List guacamole ingredients in Spanish.

learn: No me gusta nada: I don't like it at all.
check: I don't like it at all
lessons.try: Rate five foods with smiley faces and Spanish words.

learn: In many countries, lunch is the biggest meal.
check: In many Spanish-speaking countries, the biggest meal is...
lessons.try: Draw your three meals.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Food and Meals
lessons.try: Plan a fiesta menu.

learn: El bombero is the firefighter. El policía is the police officer. El cartero is the mail carrier.
El maestro teaches. El médico heals. El granjero grows food.
For women, many words end in a: la bombera, la maestra, la granjera.
lessons.try: Draw a community helper and write their job in Spanish.

learn: La escuela is the school. El hospital is the hospital. La biblioteca is the library.
El parque is the park. La tienda is the store. El mercado is the market.
Voy a la escuela means I go to school.
lessons.try: Say three places you go each week using voy a.

learn: Ayuda means helps. El bombero ayuda a la gente. The firefighter helps people.
Enseña means teaches. Cura means heals. Cocina means cooks.
lessons.try: Say what three helpers do with ayuda, enseña or cura.

learn: El bombero or la bombera: firefighter.
El policía or la policía: police officer.
lessons.try: Draw a helper and say what they do.

learn: El médico or la médica: doctor.
El veterinario or la veterinaria: vet.
lessons.try: Play vet with stuffed animals.
Write and deliver a class letter.
Map shops in a pretend town.

learn: Quiero ser maestro (I want to be a teacher).
check: Quiero ser means I want to...
Quiero ser maestra: I want to be a...
lessons.try: Draw yourself in your dream job.
Community helpers guessing game.

learn: La primavera is spring. El verano is summer. El otoño is fall. El invierno is winter.
In the desert, el verano is very hot.
Each season has its own weather and activities.
check: Which season is very hot in the desert?
lessons.try: Draw the four seasons and label them in Spanish.

learn: Hace viento means it is windy. Está nublado means it is cloudy.
Hay tormenta means there is a storm. Hay un arcoíris means there is a rainbow.
In Arizona, summer storms are called monsoons.
lessons.try: Keep a weather journal for five days in Spanish.

lessons.t: What I Do in Each Season
learn: En el verano, nado means in summer, I swim.
En el invierno, juego en la nieve means in winter, I play in the snow.
En la primavera hay flores. In spring there are flowers.
check: Juego en la nieve happens in...
lessons.try: Say one thing you do in each season.
Plant seeds and label them in Spanish.

learn: En verano voy a la playa (beach).
lessons.try: Draw a summer day.

learn: En otoño caen las hojas (leaves fall).
lessons.try: Collect leaves and name their colours.

learn: En invierno nieva en algunos lugares.
Un muñeco de nieve: a snowman.
lessons.try: Draw a snowman and label his clothes.

learn: Count the days at the end.
check: Count the sunny days at the...
lessons.try: Keep a weather graph for a week.
Season presentation.

learn: Spanish is the main language in about twenty countries.
México, Guatemala, Colombia, Perú, Chile, Argentina, España and more.
Each country has its own foods, music and special words.
check: About how many countries speak Spanish as a main language?
lessons.try: Color a map of the Spanish-speaking countries in the Americas.

learn: Mexico's flag is green, white and red with an eagle in the middle. Its capital is Ciudad de México.
Spain's capital is Madrid. Colombia's capital is Bogotá.
check: What animal is on Mexico's flag?
lessons.try: Draw the Mexican flag and label the colors in Spanish.

learn: Pick one country. Find its flag, capital and one food.
Say: Mi país es Chile. La capital es Santiago.
Sharing what we learn helps everyone learn more.
lessons.try: Make a one-page poster about a Spanish-speaking country and present it.

learn: Famous for pyramids, mariachi and tacos.
lessons.try: Draw the Mexican flag.
Find Spain on a globe.

learn: The coquí frog sings at night.
check: Puerto Rico is part of the...
lessons.try: Listen to the coquí sound.

learn: Machu Picchu is an Inca city.
check: Machu Picchu was built by the...
lessons.try: Draw Machu Picchu.
Learn a few tango steps.
Country passport project.
